bigpic.b: Asia's chip stocks crashed after Wall Street's rout
bigpic.t: with the Kospi down 5.6%, Taiwan over 6% and SoftBank 16%, erasing the rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return.
including Singapore, Malaysia, Japan and South Korea, with findings of an excess-capacity probe expected as soon as this week.
as Australia's CPI hit a three-year high of 4.9% and US PCE data due at 9:30pm SGT shapes a likely Fed hike.

stories.h: Asian stocks slump as the AI sell-off spreads, with the Kospi down 5.6%
stories.sum: South Korea's Kospi fell 5.6% to 4,725.84 in Wednesday trading, Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 3.6% to 56,502.97 and Taiwan's Taiex dropped more than 6%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the trend with a 1% gain. Nasdaq 100 futures slid 1.3% as reports of new US tariffs added to the gloom.
stories.why: A second day of AI selling suggests Monday's Huang-driven rebound was a false dawn for chip-heavy markets worldwide.

stories.h: Dow tops 50,000 while a chip rout drags the Nasdaq 1.5% lower
stories.sum: The Dow rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70 on Tuesday, led by Nike, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq fell 1.48% to 23,733.54. The Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped nearly 8% as Nvidia, AMD and Micron gave back Monday's gains.
stories.why: Money is rotating out of AI chips into consumer and industrial names, a sign investors doubt Monday's tech rebound can last.

stories.h: October PCE inflation and the Q3 GDP revision land tonight before the Thanksgiving break
stories.sum: October PCE inflation, the second estimate of third-quarter GDP and durable goods orders are due at 8:30am ET, or 9:30pm in Singapore, with October new-home sales at 10am ET. Economists expect headline PCE of 3.6% and core of 3.2%. As of 20 Nov, futures priced a 93% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike on 9 Dec.
stories.why: A hot reading would cement a 9 Dec Fed hike and add pressure on richly valued tech stocks.

stories.h: SoftBank sinks 16% and TSMC 8% as Asian chip stocks give back the Huang rally
stories.sum: SoftBank Group fell 16.1% to a 52-week low and Kioxia 15.4% in Tokyo, where Advantest lost 14.5% and Tokyo Electron 13.7%. TSMC dropped 8.1%, MediaTek 10%, Samsung Electronics 9.1% and SK Hynix 8.6%. Seoul briefly paused program trading, and Nvidia slipped another 2.2% after hours.
stories.why: Chip and AI supply-chain stocks dominate Asian indices, so a reversal this sharp shows how crowded the AI trade has become.

stories.h: HP beats on revenue but warns 2027 PC demand will shrink as memory costs climb
stories.sum: Fourth-quarter revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0B and adjusted EPS of $0.83 topped the $0.75 consensus. HP guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to $3.15 to $3.45, roughly flat, and expects 2027 PC unit demand to fall by high single to low double digits as memory and storage prices rise. It raised its quarterly dividend to $0.31.
stories.why: The AI-driven memory squeeze is now raising PC prices and cutting unit volumes across consumer hardware makers.

stories.h: Dell raises its annual revenue forecast by $10B to $202B on AI server demand
stories.sum: Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $54.9B and adjusted EPS of $9.45 beat estimates of about $6.59. Dell booked $60.2B of AI orders, lifting its AI backlog to $132.3B, and added a $25B buyback. The shares, which fell 11.83% in Tuesday's session, rose about 3% to 4% after hours.
stories.why: Shows AI infrastructure orders still accelerating despite investor jitters over valuations and spending.

stories.h: Australia's inflation jumps to a three-year high of 4.9% as power bills surge
stories.sum: Annual CPI rose to 4.9% in October from 4.3% in September, above forecasts of about 4.8%, as electricity prices jumped 25.2% after government rebates expired. The trimmed mean measure climbed to 3.8% from 3.6%. Major bank economists still expect the Reserve Bank to hold at its final 2026 meeting on 7 to 8 December.
stories.why: Stubborn price pressures limit the RBA's room to ease, keeping borrowing costs high for Australian households and lenders.

stories.h: US bank profits fall 5.9% as unrealised securities losses jump to $486B
stories.sum: FDIC-insured banks earned $84.8B in the third quarter, down 5.9% from the second quarter but up 7% from a year earlier. Unrealised losses on securities rose 48.8% to $486B, and return on assets slipped to 1.28% from 1.37%. Loans grew 1.9% in the quarter and 7.5% over the year.
stories.why: Bigger bond losses limit banks' flexibility and could bite if deposits leave, with a Fed hike ahead.

stories.h: Treasury yields dip as a $70B five-year note sale draws solid demand
stories.sum: The 10-year yield eased about 2 basis points to near 4.90% on Tuesday. The Treasury sold $70B of five-year notes at 4.719%, down from 4.845% last month, with bids worth 2.37 times the amount offered. Traders still price a 9 Dec Fed hike after New York Fed President John Williams warned inflation is too high.
stories.why: Steady demand for government debt eases fears that a hiking cycle will push long-term borrowing costs sharply higher.

stories.h: Bitcoin holds below $60,000 as tariff worries add to record ETF outflows
stories.sum: Bitcoin fell 1% to about $59,258 and ether 1.1% to about $1,661 in Asian trade on Wednesday, Reuters reported, as reports of new US tariffs on 16 economies dented risk appetite. US spot bitcoin ETFs have lost a record $4.71B so far in November. 21Shares flags $53,250, holders' average cost, as the next key level.
stories.why: Steady ETF selling shows institutions are still cutting crypto exposure as risk appetite fades across markets.

stories.h: CFTC lets futures markets count bitcoin, ether and stablecoins toward reserves
stories.sum: A 23 Nov staff advisory says swap venues, futures exchanges and clearing houses may count bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins toward the 12 months of operating costs they must hold, after valuation haircuts. The assets still do not qualify as cash or liquid securities for a separate liquidity test. The guidance is not a formal rule.
stories.why: Gives regulated derivatives firms a reason to hold crypto on their balance sheets, tying digital assets closer to US market plumbing.

stories.h: US moves to seize over $1.1B in USDC stolen in the North Korea-linked Binance hack
stories.sum: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture claim on 23 Nov for USDC tokens issued by Circle, which helped freeze them under a restraining order. North Korean hackers stole over $6B from Binance on or about 29 Oct, the department says. The US has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9B.
stories.why: Shows how freezable stablecoins can help recover stolen funds, a key argument for regulated dollar tokens.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price. It gains Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Insmed rose about 14% early and Sanofi about 5% in Paris.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: FDA approves Cogent's Ekitna for advanced GIST after it halved progression risk
stories.sum: Approved on 24 Nov with sunitinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumours that progressed after imatinib, bezuclastinib cut the risk of progression or death by half in the 413-patient PEAK trial. Median progression-free survival was 16.5 months versus 9.2 months on sunitinib alone. The label carries a boxed warning for liver toxicity.
stories.why: A first approval makes Cogent a commercial company, with two more FDA decisions in mastocytosis due by mid-2027.

stories.h: FDA clears AbbVie's Rinvoq as the first systemic treatment for nonsegmental vitiligo
stories.sum: AbbVie announced the approval on 23 Nov for patients aged 12 and older at 15mg once daily. In two Phase 3 trials of 614 patients, 23% to 25% of those on the drug regained 75% of facial pigment at 48 weeks, versus 6% to 7% on placebo. Rinvoq keeps its boxed warning on infections, cancer and heart risks.
stories.why: Opens a largely untreated skin-disease market to an oral drug, widening Rinvoq's reach across immune conditions.

stories.h: Oil slips 1.4% as supply glut worries outweigh fresh Hormuz attacks
stories.sum: Brent fell 1.4% to $90.12 a barrel and WTI 1.6% to $80.73 by late morning Wednesday in Singapore, after both rose more than 2% on Tuesday. Industry data showed US distillate stocks up 1.6M barrels, and ANZ puts Hormuz flows at 49% of normal. The IEA expects a fourth-quarter surplus.
stories.why: Traders are weighing a structural surplus against a war-hit shipping lane, leaving Asian importers and refiners exposed to big swings.

stories.h: Houthis hit a Riyadh tower as the US weighs targeting Iran's leaders, NBC reports
stories.sum: A Houthi strike on a Riyadh tower injured two Saudis and nine foreign residents, and UKMTO said three ships were hit by projectiles sailing east through Hormuz. NBC reported US officials are considering targeting Iran's senior leadership. Tehran wants the US blockade lifted, sanctions eased and frozen assets released, and the two sides remain far apart.
stories.why: Escalation beyond Hormuz would threaten Saudi supply and the Gulf shipping that Asian refiners rely on.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 baselines as Iraq rejects the capacity review
stories.sum: The 29 Nov ministerial meeting is expected to set a 2027 framework based on a commissioned assessment of members' capacity, since group-wide targets end on 31 Dec. Iraq has rejected that assessment, setting up a possible clash. Seven core members hold combined targets at 31.01M barrels a day.
stories.why: New baselines decide who can pump more next year as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: Xiaomi's profit falls 57% as EV deliveries drop and memory costs bite
stories.sum: Adjusted net profit fell 56.8% to 4.88B yuan in the third quarter, short of the 5.2B forecast, as revenue slid 5.2% to 107.24B yuan. Car deliveries fell 7.2% to 100,975 and auto revenue dropped 19.9% to 22.7B yuan, while its EV and new-business segment lost 3.4B yuan. Shares fell 3.7% in Hong Kong.
stories.why: Shows China's EV price war and the AI-driven memory squeeze hurting even the strongest new entrants.

stories.h: EU electric car sales jump 61% in October as BYD and Tesla gain ground
stories.sum: Battery-electric registrations in the EU rose 61.4% to 279,799 in October, a 29.8% share, while the overall market grew 2.6%, ACEA data show. Their year-to-date share reached 23.4%, up from 16.4%. Across the EU, EFTA and UK, BYD more than doubled to 38,755 cars and Tesla rose 76.6% to 12,116.
stories.why: Petrol and diesel are losing share fast, squeezing carmakers that have been slow to shift to electric models.

stories.h: Tesla and SpaceX name five directors to steer possible merger talks, FT reports
stories.sum: Tesla directors Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung and SpaceX's Roelof Botha and Randy Glein will guide special committees weighing an all-stock combination, the FT reported on 24 Nov. Evercore advises Tesla, and Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs advise SpaceX. Neither company commented; Bloomberg has said a deal could come as soon as December.
stories.why: A merger would tie Tesla's car business to Musk's rocket and satellite empire, changing how investors value the EV maker.

stories.h: Abercrombie, Kohl's and Dick's rally after beating forecasts before Black Friday
stories.sum: Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 20% after record third-quarter sales of $1.44B, up 11%, with comparable sales up 6%. Kohl's surged by double digits as comparable sales grew 1.2% and it raised its outlook, while Dick's lifted its adjusted EPS guidance to $11.45 to $12.30. Tariff refunds flattered several results.
stories.why: Strong reports into the holiday weekend suggest shoppers are still spending, though partly on higher prices.

stories.h: Best Buy raises its outlook after its strongest comparable sales in five years
stories.sum: Comparable sales rose 6.1% in the third quarter and revenue reached $10.24B, against $9.67B a year earlier. Adjusted EPS was $1.62. Best Buy lifted its full-year revenue forecast to $43.0B to $43.3B and comparable sales to 3.4% to 4.0%. Bespoke notes PC prices rose about 25% on memory costs while unit sales fell.
stories.why: Shoppers are absorbing electronics price rises driven by the AI memory squeeze, lifting sales in dollars rather than units.

stories.h: Dollar Tree lifts its profit outlook as shopper traffic rises 3.8%
stories.sum: Third-quarter net sales rose 6.9% to $5.07B and comparable sales grew 4.6%, driven by 3.8% more traffic. Adjusted EPS fell 4.1% to $1.16 after $0.42 of tariff-related costs. Dollar Tree raised its full-year adjusted EPS forecast to $8.05 to $8.25, including about $0.65 of tariff refunds.
stories.why: More shoppers trading down to discounters points to strained household budgets heading into the holidays.

stories.h: Netflix buys Los Angeles' Radford Studio Center for $380M
stories.sum: Netflix bought the 55-acre Studio City lot, which has 22 stages, directly from Goldman Sachs-led lenders who took it from Hackman Capital Partners, which paid $1.85B in 2021. The streamer plans renovations and will keep the studio team, calling the purchase a meaningful new investment in California's film industry.
stories.why: Distressed studio lots are changing hands far below peak prices, letting streamers lock in production space cheaply.

stories.h: Disney's Hexed and Universal's Focker In-Law open into a key Thanksgiving test
stories.sum: Both films open on Wednesday. Deadline's early forecasts put each at $40M to $50M over five days, though Box Office Theory has cut Hexed to about $23M. The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping, which opened to an estimated $120M, could top both in its second weekend.
stories.why: Thanksgiving is a major test for cinemas after the five-day haul fell to $290.3M in 2025 from $424.9M in 2024.

stories.h: Skydance merges Warner Bros. TV and Paramount TV studios into one unit
stories.sum: The combined Warner Bros. Television Studios, launching in early 2027, will pool more than 120 franchises including The Pitt and Ted Lasso. Former Netflix executives Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell will run it as co-presidents under George Cheeks. CBS Studios stays separate, and further layoffs are possible.
stories.why: Hollywood consolidation is shrinking the number of major studio buyers, squeezing writers, producers and suppliers.

stories.h: Malaysia Airlines orders 10 Boeing 787s to replace its A350s from 2032
stories.sum: Malaysia Aviation Group signed for 10 787 Dreamliners with options for six more at a Kuala Lumpur ceremony attended by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Deliveries run from 2032 to 2035, gradually replacing its seven A350s. The GEnx-powered jets will seat 319 in three classes on routes such as London, Sydney and Tokyo. No value was disclosed.
stories.why: Another Asian widebody win for Boeing, though 2030s delivery dates show how long airlines must wait for new jets.

stories.h: Boeing lands a 50-jet 737 MAX order worth $7.4B from China's Xiamen Airlines
stories.sum: Xiamen Airlines, a China Southern unit, will buy 50 737 MAX 8 jets valued at $7.4B at list prices, before discounts, with deliveries from 2031 to 2034. The deal still needs shareholder and government approval. China pledged at the May Trump-Xi summit to buy 200 Boeing jets; it is unclear whether this order counts toward that.
stories.why: Signals China reopening to Boeing after trade-war curbs on deliveries, a key market for its narrowbody jets.

stories.h: FAA braces for its busiest Thanksgiving in 16 years, with 417,775 flights planned
stories.sum: The FAA expects 417,775 flights over the nine days to 1 Dec, up 2.2% on last year and 7.5% on 2019, with Tuesday the peak at more than 52,000. The TSA expects nearly 17.6 million passengers from Tuesday to Monday, and airlines nearly 29 million over 20 to 30 Nov.
stories.why: A smooth holiday would ease pressure on the air traffic system after the 13 Nov ground stop disrupted more than 18,000 flights.

stories.h: US home price growth stalls at 2.1% as monthly prices slip in 17 of 20 cities
stories.sum: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller national index rose 2.1% from a year earlier in September, unchanged from August, but fell 0.3% on the month. The 20-city index gained 2.6%, below the 2.7% expected. Chicago led at 6.9% while Seattle fell 1.9%. The FHFA index rose 2.5%.
stories.why: Home prices are now rising more slowly than 3.7% inflation, eroding owners' real equity while mortgage rates stay high.

stories.h: US housing braces for a harsh winter as sales slump
stories.sum: Pending home sales were down nearly 17% from a year earlier in October, and MBA purchase applications ran 18% below last year in mid-November. Real REMAX expects 2027 existing-home sales to fall 5% to 10% and national prices 3% to 4%.
stories.why: With 30-year mortgage rates near 7.1% and a Fed hike coming, a quick recovery looks unlikely.

stories.h: Mortgage rates at 7.28% push existing-home sales to a decade low
stories.sum: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate reached 7.28% in the survey released 19 November, up from 7.11% a week earlier, with the next reading brought forward to Wednesday by the holiday. The National Association of Realtors said October existing-home sales ran at an annual 3.75 million, the weakest pace since 2010.
stories.why: Borrowing costs at their highest since 2000 are freezing out buyers and squeezing agents, builders and lenders.

stories.h: US readies new tariffs on 16 economies, including Singapore and Malaysia
stories.sum: Findings of a Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity could come as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, Reuters reported, citing three people. The 16 include China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore. Rates are unclear; the duties would partly replace levies the Supreme Court struck down in February.
stories.why: Fresh duties would hit the region's export-driven electronics makers just as AI-led trade is lifting growth.

stories.h: Malaysia tells data centres not to serve the seven firms on the new US chip blacklist
stories.sum: MIDA will advise all operators not to host, lease space to or provide services to the entities the US added on 23 Nov. MITI says only Speedmatrix and MSFusion are registered in Malaysia; Speedmatrix is owned by Singapore-incorporated Megaspeed International. MITI says Malaysia will not be used to get around export controls.
stories.why: Kuala Lumpur is moving fast to shield its US-chip-dependent data-centre boom from wider American penalties.

stories.h: Singapore lifts 2026 growth forecast to about 6% after Q3 GDP jumps 6.1%
stories.sum: Third-quarter growth was revised up to 6.1% year on year from a 5.4% advance estimate, beating forecasts of 5.6%, led by AI-driven electronics output and wholesale trade. The trade ministry raised its 2026 forecast from 4.5% to 5.5% to around 6%, and expects 2.5% to 4.5% growth in 2027.
stories.why: Confirms AI exports are powering Singapore, though officials warn a turn in the AI cycle could hit markets hard.

stories.h: StarHub and M1 agree an all-share merger creating a S$5B Singapore telco
stories.sum: StarHub will issue about 651.7 million new shares, 27.4% of the enlarged group, to M1's owners, giving the combination an enterprise value of S$5B (US$3.87B). Keppel, which owns about 84% of M1, will hold 23%. The firms target S$110M of yearly cost savings by 2030; completion is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to IMDA approval.
stories.why: Consolidation in Singapore's crowded mobile market could ease price competition and lift returns for the remaining operators.
